action.rationale: Budget 100 is < 20×dim (300), so run limited probes (P1–P3) to learn global structure without spending much (≈12% = 12 evals). This will tell us if a fast local polish or a global method (TuRBO/CMA-ES) is appropriate on this 15-D problem.

Probes show weak global structure (P2 fdc_spearman=0.27, top10_spread_vs_uniform=0.97), so we hedge between a population method and a model-based method. With dim=15 and only 88 evals left of 100, a small race (18 evals ≈ 20% of total) will pick the more sample-efficient approach.

Turbo won the race decisively (1979.94 vs 3178.25) and hasn’t actually run yet (evals_in_tenure=0, tr_length=0.8). With a small total budget (100 < 30·dim) and weak global structure indicated by P2 fdc=0.27 and top10_spread_vs_uniform≈0.97, TuRBO is the most sample-efficient choice now.
